classification.description: An extremely fast Python linter and code formatter, written in Rust.

plan.architecture_summary: Ruff is an extremely fast Python linter and code formatter written in Rust, structured as a monorepo with flat crates located in the `crates/` directory. The core linting logic, rules, and checkers live primarily in `crates/ruff_linter`, while the command-line interface lives in `crates/ruff`. Other crates handle AST representation (`ruff_python_ast`), formatting (`ruff_python_formatter`), semantic analysis, and development utilities. Development relies on Cargo for building and testing, `uv` for Python tooling and running utility commands, and `cargo insta` for snapshot testing.

commit: Include category and rule code/name in PR titles for lint rules (e.g. `[flake8-simplify] Fix key_in_dict for keys method (SIM118)`)
pull_request: Follow PR template summary and notes, and adhere to Astral's AI policy.
code_style: prek run --all-files via uv (formatting and Markdown/Python linting)

issues.title: Use the indent-width setting for E111 and E114
issues.why: A well-scoped configuration issue ideal for a Rust beginner looking at pycodestyle rules.
issues.approach: Update E111 and E114 checks in `crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/pycodestyle/rules/logical_lines/indentation.rs` to respect the configured indent-width setting.

issues.title: `N999` (`invalid-module-name`) mixes correctness and stylistic recommendations
issues.why: Gives exposure to naming rules and separation of module name correctness versus style in `pep8_naming`.
issues.approach: Review N999 module name validation logic in `crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/pep8_naming/rules/invalid_module_name.rs` to separate correctness checks from stylistic recommendations.

issues.title: Ruff --fix on SIM118 introducing TypeError
issues.why: Targets a specific rule logic file in `flake8_simplify` with a clear bug report and minimal reproduction example.
issues.approach: Examine SIM118 implementation in `crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/flake8_simplify/rules/key_in_dict.rs` to ensure `--fix` does not incorrectly flag or transform objects with a `.keys()` method but no `__iter__` or incorrect type.

issues.title: F841 treats `except` bindings differently from all other bindings
issues.why: Directly points to the file and function handling unused variables in bindings, making it a great target for understanding Ruff's semantic analysis.
issues.approach: Investigate how `except` bindings are handled separately in `crates/ruff_linter/src/checkers/ast/analyze/bindings.rs` and refactor them to be processed consistently with other bindings to avoid false positives in F841.

first_timer_insights: First-time contributors often start by tackling `good first issue` or `help wanted` items related to specific lint rules, configuration handling, or bug fixes in `ruff_linter`.
caveats: Ensure the Rust toolchain and `uv` are installed before running development tasks. Some rules or snapshot tests may require `cargo insta review` after making modifications.
